producer_report.summary: Added crates/athena-core/src/role_need.rs and wired it into `athena status` as `role need` lines. Root cause of the earlier blocker: the retire rule read runs only from job invocations, but steward, audience and auditor runs are stored in separate Records lists (steward_runs, audience_runs, auditor_runs). compute_at now collects runs for every role from all jobs' invocations plus those three lists. A role is a retire candidate only if it has runs on record, none in the last 14 days, and the window holds at least 5 runs of any role. A role with no recorded run, or judged in a thin window, is shown `not measured`. Classes: the newest 10 closed request jobs per class are used; a class with at least 4 jobs, at least 3 failures and at least half failed is listed as `needed`. Failed/Rejected/TimedOut count as failed; Declined/Closed are excluded. StatusView gains `role_need` and STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS gains ("role need","role_need"); display.rs prints the lines. OLY-9-11 now names role_need.rs and ends `status: role need`. CHANGELOG entry added. ALL_ROLES did not exist, so I defined it in role_need.rs.

open_issues: Window of 14 days, minimum of 5 window runs, 10 jobs per class, 3 failures and at least half failed are my choices, not from a spec; tune if the owner prefers.
Failures are attributed to a class, not to a specific role, so `needed` is advice about a class of work.
mistakes: My first draft of the ordering test renamed job ids in a convoluted way; I simplified it before the first run.
learnings: ALL_ROLES did not exist in the code; the Role enum has 8 variants.
StatusView is Serialize only and has no Default, so the display test builds every field by hand.
status::planning_cost_tests::invocation is a pub(crate) test fixture that other core tests can reuse.
The `Job` record can be built in tests from a JSON stub with class_of_work set.
